title: Weekly build slice orchestration + Stable/LTS promotion runbook
creator: Ava Patel
description: Design and implement a deterministic weekly 'slice' cut process that produces one candidate RC per week, exercises staged promotion to stable and LTS channels, and automates release notes. The runbook will codify pre-cut health checks, gating metrics, artifact tagging conventions, and rollback steps for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Focus areas: gating for KV cache/continuous batching regressions, deterministic RC tagging from release branch, release-notes generation from PR labels and CHANGELOG entries, and clear upgrade tooling notes for Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible CI workflow that produces a single RC artifact every Thursday UTC with deterministic semver metadata
Automated gating job that fails the cut if critical e2e smoke or latency regressions exceed thresholds
Release notes generated automatically from merged PR labels and changelog fragments and uploaded to the release page
Promotion job that can move an RC -> stable; and stable -> LTS with one-click approval and audit trail
Runbook pages and on-call playbook created and reviewed by SRE/PM/Design
steps: Pre-cut: run smoke suite against canary on dedicated pool, verify 99th-p50 latency within 5% of baseline, warm KV cache sample workloads
CI: create slice branch from main, run full integration and canary bench; produce RC artifact (sha+buildmeta) and upload to artifacts registry
Tagging: lightweight automation applies rc-YYYYMMDD+NN semver metadata, signs artifact, and creates release draft in console/internal-releases
Gates: gating job aggregates e2e, perf, and infra checks; failures require triage and either hotfix or cut deferral
Release notes: parse PR labels (feature/bugfix/security/changelog) and CHANGELOG fragments, assemble markdown, attach to release draft
Promotion: scheduled canary rollout to 10% in us-west, 30% eu-west after 2 hours if no regressions, then promote to stable; LTS promotion requires >=3 stable weekly releases plus security signoff
Rollback: automatic fallback policy to previous stable with preserved KV cache compatibility flag; runbook documents manual rollback steps for private deployments

rollout_plan: Begin with a staggered canary: 5% traffic on non-critical shard for 2h, 10% global for 4h, measure error-rate, end-to-end latency, and token generation cost delta. If regressions are below thresholds, expand to 50% across regions for 12h. Stable promotion requires 48h of green at 50% plus SRE signoff. LTS promotion requires 3 consecutive weekly stable releases and security/compliance signoff. Promotion tooling will record audit metadata (who approved, timestamp, prerequisite checks) and allow a single-click rollback to prior stable with metrics snapshot.
notes_for_oncall: On-call should monitor release-health dashboard for the first 6 hours after cut. Alerts: error-rate > 0.2% above baseline, token cost delta > 12%, KV cache miss rate spike > 15%. If any alert fires, pause promotion and escalate to release lead (Diego). For private deployments, contact solutions-eng with upgrade window and provide pre-flight config checklist.
changelog_strategy: Require PR authors to include a single-line changelog fragment with label changelog/{major,minor,patch}. CI will enforce presence of changelog label and generate a structured changelog by grouping fragments. Security fixes must include label 'security' and are surfaced first in release notes. Release notes will contain API-impact section, migration instructions for private/dedicated customers, and links to rollback steps.
operational_risks: Perf flakiness for long-seq test causing false-negative gates
KV cache warming may cause higher first-token cost impacting canary metrics
Private upgrade orchestration variability across customer environments
